notes.title: Gear Overhaul & One Year Update
notes.content: [p]  Well hey there stranger! Long time no see. Today marks a whole [i]YEAR[/i] since we launched into Early Access.. and a whopping eight months since our last public update. Now, a lot of you have been playing on our Beta branch since February, but there's plenty new here for that lot as well. So let me shed some light on what's been going on at the Lab:[/p][p][/p][p]  Following our 'Physics Update' last October, we got straight to work on a modular board setup so players could customize more than just colors. In refactoring the board setup we created a LOT more work for ourselves & had to essentially rework every system in the game to accommodate.. and while doing that I revisited the question [i]"should we add a skater?"[/i] since doing so would likely require similar reworks.[/p][p]  After poking around the concept for about a week, we had some promising (yet very janky) results and decided to go all in. That was in mid-december - and since then a ton of work has gone into just making everything fit together again. While most of those changes have been to the back-end of things, we haven't slept on improving some things that were lacking in audio, physics & mechanics, and even some new game modes. It breaks down about like this:[/p][p][/p][h1][b]Characters & Gear[/b][/h1][h3][b]a complete overhaul[/b][/h3][p][/p][h2][b]Characters[/b][/h2][p]First, a disclaimer.. We've gone all in on a [i]system[/i] that includes selectable and customizable characters, but haven't fleshed out things like animation & full customization. Hence, the simple 'Human' & 'Hand' characters are marked as Beta features with very basic color customization. Beyond those, the classic 'Ghost' character still benefits from the new system with motion to the ankles and the ability to walk around off-board. We've kept our Slip Ons & Mid Tops with a handful of new sock options.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Gear[/b][/h2][p]At last, the board setup is fully modular. Pick from a handful of skate AND fingerboard decks, grip, trucks, and wheels at different shapes, sizes, & colors. Build your ideal setup, mix & match to put together something different. Naturally, each setup will skate slightly different - things like deck sizes, truck widths, wheel sizes, wheel base, will make differences not unlike what you'd feel irl.[/p][h3][b]Board Wear[/b][/h3][p]Deck and Trucks wear & tear as you skate, and can be reset from the Gear Menu with R3.[/p][h3][b]Profiles[/b][/h3][p]We're introducing 3 different board profiles you can easily swap between. Just press X/Square in the gear menu to select & customize one of the three.[/p][p][/p][h1][b]Physics & Mechanics[/b][/h1][h3][b]Improved stability, refinement[/b][/h3][p][/p][list][*][p][b]Crouch & Prewind[/b][/p][p]This is now integral to the pop mechanic. To crouch in regular stance, pull your front foot towards the center of the board. The further you pull back, the more you crouch & the higher you'll pop. While crouching, pull either trigger to prewind for a quicker rotation off the pop.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Auto Catch[/b][/p][p]There's now an Auto Catch stat which, when enabled, will catch the board if your trick input is complete (both sticks return to center) and the board is oriented grip-up and aligned with your rotation.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Boned Ollies[/b][/p][p]Moving both sticks forward or backward during ollies will extend the legs into a boned ollie position.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Auto Revert[/b][/p][p]When enabled, this will apply a momentary torque upon landing to align the board with your movement direction, resulting in improved stability & flow.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Reworked Powerslides[/b][/p][p]Powerslides (both sticks inward or outward while on ground) have been reworked to limit the sideways angle & return once released. Add trigger input to continue into reverts.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Grind Stabilization[/b][/p][p]Huge improvements to grind stabilization, and a corresponding Stat (0-10) to adjust intensity. This makes grinds much less likely to slip off.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Improved Flip axis & stability[/b][/p][p]Particularly, kickflips and heelflips flip more consistently on-axis. Still as before though, their leveling and rotation is highly dependent on input timing and direction. My personal tip: The ideal timing is likely later than you think![/p][/*][*][p][b]Truck Stiffness[/b][/p][p]Adjust your turning sensitivity with a new Truck Stiffness Stat (1-5)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Push Type[/b][/p][p]Players can now choose between a single push force, or the classic continuous push (more analogous to fingerboarding)[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Reworked Audio[/b][/h2][p]New sounds that reflect irl skateboarding on a variety of surface types - Concrete, Wood, Metal, and Grass[/p][p][/p][h2][b]New Game Mode - Skill Games[/b][/h2][p]From the Maps Menu you'll find the Rat Race obstacle courses! These are prototype levels that work to 'gamify' our mechanics for a little something different. In the future you can expect some different types of Skill Games with things like physics puzzles, time trials, etc.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]UI[/b][/h2][list][*][p]Replay Diagnostics - Press D on your keyboard while in replay to load a diagnostics visualizer, which shows the board control forces at play during playback.[/p][/*][*][p]Descriptions have been added to relevant Stats[/p][/*][*][p]Gameplay tips added to Pause menu[/p][/*][*][p]Control Overlay & Haptics Toggles now live in the Options Menu[/p][/*][*][p]Replay UI has been updated for improved clarity[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2][b]Multiplayer[/b][/h2][p]Unfortunately Multiplayer is still under maintenance following structural changes, and is temporarily disabled from the Pause menu. In its current development state we have the board replicating properly as before, but character/animation replication needs more work. Peer to Peer multiplayer should still work fine on the Pre-Character branch.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Beta Branches[/b][/h2][p]Moving forward, we'll maintain our Beta branches publicly with the option to stay on the main public branch, roll back to previous branches, or follow the latest beta builds. From SkateLab's properties in steam, just navigate to the Betas tab & choose a specific game version.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]What's Next?[/b][/h2][p]Looking forward, we'll continue to put a strong focus on physics & mechanics; adding some needed content - new maps & map extensions; and fleshing out character animation & customization. Having gone through the entire project with a fine-toothed comb - it's more organized than ever under the hood, and we're able to move more flexibly and quickly.[/p][p][/p][p]THANK YOU for reading, for playing, and here's to another year of progress![/p][p]- Van[/p]

notes.title: Physics & Replay Update
notes.content:
Hey hey hey! So we've been focused hard on physics for the last month or so & made BIG progress on some core mechanics. Is the work done? Not by a long shot.. but things are moving in the right direction and we're excited to share where we're at.

We had a lot of goals going into this update & one of the most crucial was to soften the learning curve for new & existing players by making board control overall more intuitive. To that end, we have two new stats - Auto Level & Grind Stabilization - as well as a handful of physics refinements.

Along with these changes, we've filled in some large gaps in the Replay System! Replays now have sounds, slomo, and keyframing; PLUS you can see your control overlay in replay & watch your precise inputs throughout gameplay.

With that said & without any more fluff, here's a more complete list of what's new:

[h3][b]Stats & Physics/Mechanics[/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] Added [b]Auto Level[/b] - [i]this will have the most drastic effect on gameplay. With it on, ollies will self-level to an extent, and stick movements will tweak/shifty in air. This means an ollie can be done with a single stick & in-air control is much more predictable.[/i]
[*] Added new [b]Grind Stabilization[/b] - [i]this does not 'magnetize' grinds at all - it uses similar code to auto level & tries to keep the board upright during grinds. L3/R3 hold during grinds isn't necessary for stability, but still can be used to disable pop[/i]
[*] Added [b]Gravity Multiplier[/b] to stats
[*] Added [b]Stomp Catch to stats[/b] - [i]this already existed, but can now be toggled OFF if desired. When enabled, hold both L3 & R3 when catching to stomp[/i]
[*] Added [b]Reset to Default[/b] option to stats
[*] Added [b]trails to input overlay[/b]
[*] Stick input mappings have been refined & should result in far fewer instances of feet 'hopping' unintentionally.
[*] Pop is now more reliant on [b]Input Speed[/b] - [i]popping faster will pop higher, slower will pop lower.[/i]
[*] [b]Shuvits[/b] & variations now rotate on a more level plane
[*] [b]Manuals[/b] no longer require L3/R3 input to balance steadily
[*] [b]Stats have been reset[/b] - New stats may not match 1:1 with old stats if set to the same values
[*] Flicks have become more sensitive to [b]timing[/b] - [i]whether a kickflip flips straight, or skews fs/bs relies on timing, direction, & input speed. This is more a byproduct of other changes & will continue to be worked on.[/i]
[*] Scoop+Flick combinations still are a big thorn in our side.. after several attempts to solve for better tre flips, hardflips etc.. nothing *so far* has been the solution I'm looking for. This continues to be a high priority moving forward.
[*] Feet now rotate based on their current state & player input for [b]more natural looking movement during tricks[/b]
[/list]


[h3][b]Replay System[/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] Added [b]Slomo[/b] playback
[*] Added [b]Sounds[/b] to playback
[*] Added [b]Input Overlay[/b] (L3 + R3 to toggle)
[*] [b]Keyframes[/b] for [b]cam position & play rate[/b] have been added - [i]follow on-screen UI for usage instructions, I'll also try to put out some kind of explainer in the coming days.[/i]
[*] [b]note:[/b] Keyframes only play in [b]Playback Camera[/b] (switch cameras using X/Square)
[*] Replay now begins at your last respawn, & all respawns create keys you can quickly navigate using dpad left/right
[/list]


[h3][b]Known Bugs[/b][/h3]

New progress = new bugs. Here are a few that have our attention right now:
[list]
[*] if in Multiplayer & Replay, skaters who are not also in replay will only update when your board isn't moving
[*] if in Multiplayer & exiting replay, it can take a few moments for your board to reappear.. until that time you'll be invisible
[*] Tricks out of grinds are slightly less predictable. Some parts of the grind & tricking systems will need reworking to handle this properly.
[/list]

Oh also, we expanded the Amphitheater map a bit. Enjoy!

notes.title: Object Dropper Update
notes.content:
[b]Hi there![/b]

Since our last update, we've been set on making progress with SkateLab's Object Dropper. Our primary goals were to add the abilities to spawn new objects, and to save & load map layouts.. and of course to add more placeable objects to the game. This necessitated reworking a lot of the object dropper's back-end to enable more flexibility for us and modders. In the time it took to do that, we managed to accomplish a few more things.. and today we're stoked to be sharing the progress with you! Here's a (mostly) full list of what's new:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033232/190229a6f37f7dd9eaf4781790a40eeaee50c2e4.png[/img]

[b]New Content[/b]

[list]
[*] Added new map - [b]The Flat[/b]
[*] Added new "shoes" - [b]Fingertips[/b]
[*] Added new [b]Create & Skate layout[/b] to include many of our new placeable objects
[/list]

[b]Object Dropper[/b]

[list]
[*] Added ability to [b]spawn new objects[/b] (press X/Square while in Object Dropper with no object selected)
[*] Added ability to [b]save & load object layouts[/b] (press Start button while in Object Dropper)
[*] Added a number of [b]new placeable objects[/b] to the system
[*] Added new [b]options for placeable lights[/b]
[*] Added ability to [b]Add & Remove points from Shapeable objects[/b]
[*] Added [b]movement speed adjustment[/b] (Dpad Left/Right)
[*] Added [b]camera zoom adjustment[/b] (LB + LS up/down)
[*] Changed [b]ground snapping to an on/off toggle[/b] where the object will snap to ground while moving
[*] Changed Z axis rotation from world space to local space
[*] Added ability for modders to add their own custom objects as placeables in a similar way to adding custom maps currently. (Custom objects will be added to their own tab in the Spawn Object menu, tutorial coming soon)
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45033232/e82d4c24730f6d14fd99f86d6fc75fab6a1adf10.png[/img]

[b]Physics[/b]

[list]
[*] Changed the board's Collision bodies to more closely match its actual shape. This is most noticeable during scooped tricks, which previously would pop in unpredictable directions from hitting sharp corners.
[*] Changed ollie leveling torque pivot, resulting in slightly more natural in-air movement
[/list]

[b]Performance Optimization[/b]

[list]
[*] Added LODs to the board & many objects resulting in a significant performance improvement across the game
[*] Reworked collision in Amphitheater map, which was previously causing some hang ups & lag
[/list]

[b]Misc[/b]

[list]
[*] Replaced 'Long' camera preset with 'High' preset
[/list]

[b]Known Bugs[/b]

[list]
[*] If MP host cancels from moving an object, said object has no collision for clients until placed again
[/list]


[b]For a reminder on how to enter the Object Dropper:[/b] you can enter Board Placement at any time by pressing Y/Triangle - from Board Placement mode, press X/Square to enter Object Dropper & follow the on-screen UI to manipulate objects & create your own spots. We hope you'll enjoy these changes!


[b]What's next?[/b]

Over the time we took working on these features, we've had a lot of new ideas about Physics & Mechanics - so that's where our focus will be pointed in the coming weeks - and we're hyped for it. Along with that, we've already been putting some effort into exploring new game modes & adding in-game tutorials. It's a strong goal of ours to not only improve our mechanics, but to better teach these mechanics to new players, and keep gameplay fun & engaging for those returning to the Lab.

notes.title: The Ditch & Mod Maps
notes.content:
[b]Howdy Lab Rats![/b]

This is our first update since launching into early access - we've had some fantastic feedback and lots of movement within our growing community. Today we're happy to be adding some much needed content to the game. Here's what's new:

[b]New Features[/b]

[list]
[*] New Map - [b]The Ditch[/b]
[*] Added [b]Map Preview Images[/b]
[*] Added [b]Radial Menu[/b] for Emotes & Lighting Control (Hold LB & navigate using sticks/dpad)
[*] Added Emotes: [b]Fire, Sunglasses, Surprise,[/b] and [b]Rain Cloud[/b]
[/list]

[list]
[*] Added a [b]Community Maps list[/b] (appears in maps menu when custom maps are present)
[/list]

[b]Multiplayer[/b]

[list]
[*] Added [b]Map Name to server list[/b]
[*] Added [b]Player Joined/Left[/b] notification
[*] Added [b]Player list[/b] to menu while in Multiplayer
[*] Added [b]Object Dropper ability for Host[/b] in Multiplayer
[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]

[list]
[*] Fixed SloMo speed adjustment in Multiplayer
[*] Fixed Bearing sound changing pitch while in Board Placement
[*] Fixed rolling backward when exiting Board Placement
[*] Fixed camera positioning bugs in Replay
[*] Fixed duplicates in Object Dropper spawning with default scale & settings
[*] More small tweaks & bug fixes
[/list]

With a rapidly developing modding community, we should also note that there's a new [b]Modding Discord[/b] server, where you'll find a growing number of shoes, deck graphics, maps, and more on the way!

[url=https://discord.gg/KCBqkmbhvc]Modding Discord[/url]
[url=https://discord.gg/eWumGYUtZ6]Official Discord[/url]

Happy shredding,
Van
